cover letter
Bachelor’s degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience or training, ideally in hospitality or event coordination.
Experience training, scheduling, coaching, or providing day-to-day direction to employees or volunteers.

Under the supervision of the Director of Events & Revenue, the Event Operations Coordinator manages the event pipeline for university, nonprofit, and external clients and coordinates a portfolio of smaller and less complex events. The role serves as the primary client contact for assigned events and the onsite representative when the Director is absent. The Event Operations Coordinator supports the planning and execution of weddings and other complex events. The Event Operations Coordinator is a hands-on role for an organized, service-minded professional who enjoys both the details behind the scenes and the energy of event day. The Event Operations Coordinator owns a portfolio of events from inquiry through closeout, builds client and vendor relationships, leads a small team of student employees, and helps refine the systems that keep a growing events program running smoothly while contributing to the Center's revenue. Pricing exceptions, refunds, material contract changes, and higher-risk decisions are escalated to the Director.
Comfort using CRM, scheduling, database, spreadsheet, and shared-document systems, along with basic event budgeting, purchasing, payment tracking, and financial record keepingpractices.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work primarily on campus, with periods of remote work possible based on operational needs. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.
Will be required to wear a University provided uniform.

Employees whose positions are designated as Category 1 or Category 2 for occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM) must receive the Hepatitis B vaccination or sign a Hepatitis B vaccination declination statement. Initial and annual Bloodborne Pathogens training is also required.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple events / projects concurrently, establish priorities, maintain schedules, and meet firm deadlines.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.

Strong client-service and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build positive working relationships with clients, campus partners, vendors, guests, students, and colleagues from diverse backgrounds.
Ability to walk multiple nightly rounds on uneven surfaces and repeatedly climb stairs.
Good organizational skills.

Must have the ability to: operate a vacuum, floor scrubber, and polisher; use cleaning chemical compounds; perform essential custodial duties including dumping bags into dumpster or moving equipment and materials with or without accommodations.
Ability to effectively communicate with diverse audiences in writing.
Ability to ascend/descend ladders with or without accommodation.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate, organized, and complete records and documentation.
Ability to safely perform the physical requirements necessary to move light to moderate objects up to 60 lbs., with or without accommodation.
Ability to work independently, anticipate needs, exercise sound judgment, and solve event-day problems with calm and professionalism.
Ability to work a variable schedule including evenings and weekends.
Knowledge of basic event budgeting, purchasing, payment tracking, and financial recordkeeping practices.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
